# No Jensen, No Problem? NVIDIA Delivers Strong Outlook, Rules Out Huang’s Return

**NVIDIA Corp.** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA)[(NASDAQ:NVDA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA) stock rose nearly 4% in Wednesday’s premarket session as investors reacted to stronger-than-expected quarterly results and an [upbeat growth outlook](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/11/63372441/nvidia-stock-jumps-on-q3-double-beat-strong-outlook-explosive-demand-for-vera-rubin).

A broader recovery in technology stocks also supported the gains. Nasdaq futures rose 0.94%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.46%.

The chipmaker’s quarterly results and strong artificial intelligence demand helped ease concerns about its near-term performance.

However, NVIDIA continues to face leadership uncertainty and regulatory scrutiny. Investors are weighing the company’s growth prospects against succession, China exposure [and financing risks](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/11/63356810/why-nvidia-is-falling-tuesday-jensen-huangs-comeback-statement-congress-hearings-and-ai-risks).

## Kress Seen As Steady Interim Leader

**D.A. Davidson** Managing Director **Gil Luria** [told](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/18/arms-rene-haas-leads-nvidia-ceo-race-but-company-ties-could-be-hurdle.html) CNBC on Wednesday that interim CEO **Colette Kress** can guide NVIDIA through the transition because she knows the business well. Still, he does not view her or other insiders as ideal permanent candidates while investigations into Asian sales continue.

Luria called **Arm Holdings Plc** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ARM)[(NASDAQ:ARM)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ARM) CEO **Rene Haas** the leading external candidate because of his semiconductor experience and familiarity with NVIDIA, while also naming **Apple Inc.** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AAPL)[(NASDAQ:AAPL)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AAPL) hardware chief **Johny Srouji** and **Broadcom Inc.** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AVGO)[(NASDAQ:AVGO)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AVGO) executive **Charlie Kawwas** as potential alternatives.

**Futurum** analyst **Rolf Bulk** [also](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/18/nvidia-transition-chip-development-create-openings-for-rivals-futurum.html) described Haas as a top contender. However, he said NVIDIA would still need to reorganize reporting lines and rebuild some of the relationships Huang personally managed.

## Strong Results Ease Near-Term Demand Concerns

After NVIDIA’s quarterly report, Luria said demand remained strong enough for the company to raise its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to 75% from 70%, even as it acknowledged uncertainty around Asian sales.

**Susquehanna** analyst **Chris Rolland** called the quarter a “very solid report” and [told](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/nvidia-out-with-very-solid-report-says-susquehannas-chris-rolland.html) CNBC that Kress and board chair **Harvey Jones** were doing a strong job establishing stability.

**Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster** [told](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/sec-investigation-an-expected-outcome-for-nvidia-says-deepwaters-gene-munster.html) CNBC that he viewed NVIDIA’s decision to guide as particularly bullish because Kress put her name behind the outlook despite the leadership turmoil and new export restrictions.

**StoneX** analyst **Cody Acree** [also](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/nvidia-board-will-likely-stick-to-decision-regarding-jensen-huang-says-stonexs-cody-acree.html) described the results as solid across revenue, guidance and gross margin.

## Kress Says Demand And Supply Remain Strong

Kress told CNBC that customer demand for NVIDIA’s computing infrastructure continues to rise and that expanded supply across chips, advanced packaging and memory supported the higher growth forecast.

She also rejected concerns about a widespread employee exodus, saying leadership and staff remain focused on executing the company’s roadmap.

Kress [told](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/watch-jim-cramers-full-interview-with-nvidia-interim-ceo-colette-kress.html) CNBC that NVIDIA plans to continue stock repurchases, with \$277 billion available, while maintaining disciplined investments across the AI ecosystem.

## Financing Strategy May Become More Selective

Bulk expects NVIDIA to scrutinize new neocloud financing deals more closely while continuing to support existing customers such as **CoreWeave** **Inc.** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CRWV)[(NASDAQ:CRWV)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CRWV) and **OpenAI**.

Before the results, **Cantor Fitzgerald** analyst **C.J. Muse** [told](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/cantor-fitzgeraldas-cj-muse-on-nvidia-interim-ceo-kress-likely-to-reiterate-70-percent-growth-for-2027.html) CNBC on Tuesday that he expected NVIDIA to temper its investment levels, potentially forcing some neocloud partners to seek more outside financing.

However, Rolland said NVIDIA’s post-earnings disclosures suggested the company was still “leaning into” financing commitments rather than withdrawing broadly.

## Huang Return Appears Unlikely

Former CEO **Jensen Huang** said he would be willing to return if NVIDIA’s board asked him to, but Kress said the board “will not reinstate Jensen.”

Rolland also said he does not expect Huang to return as CEO, though he believes NVIDIA could benefit from using him as an outside strategic or technical adviser.

**Wolfe Research** analyst **Chris Caso**, in a CNBC [interview](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/jensen-huang-faces-tough-road-if-he-returns-to-nvidia-wolfe-researchs-caso.html) on Tuesday, similarly described Huang’s path back as difficult, given precedent involving CEOs and relationships with employees.

## Investigations Remain A Major Overhang

NVIDIA continues to face scrutiny over sales through Asia and potential access to restricted chips.

Luria estimates that 5% to 20% of NVIDIA chip sales may have reached China directly or through resellers and Asian data centers, which drove his price-target reduction to \$200 from \$300, despite maintaining a Buy rating.

Munster called the reported SEC investigation an “expected outcome” of the turmoil and said the central financial risk is whether tighter Asian restrictions reduce revenue.

Despite those concerns, analysts broadly viewed NVIDIA’s underlying demand and product roadmap as resilient.

**NVDA Price Action:** NVIDIA shares were up 3.69% at \$161.19 during premarket trading on Wednesday, [according to Benzinga Pro data](https://www.benzinga.com/pro/register-3).
